description:
Music for a Heavy Heart | Sarangi | Indian Classical

You've been holding it together all day. Maybe longer than that.

This is for the heaviness you haven't had room to put down — the heartache, the grief, the thing that sits in your chest and doesn't lift just because the day asked you to keep moving. You don't have to push it down here. The Sarangi is the most human-sounding of all Indian instruments — bowed, voiced, it slides and sighs like a voice on the edge of tears. It sounds like crying so you don't have to carry it in alone.

This is 90 minutes of solo Sarangi in Raga Puriya — a deep evening raga of pathos and introspective longing. There's no rhythm, no tabla, no place you need to be. Just the bow drawing out long, weeping phrases, and the tanpura holding the room open underneath. Let it sit with you. Let the tears come if they want to.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Sarangi — bowed gut strings, the most vocal and human of Indian instruments, sliding meend that mimics a crying voice
- Raga Puriya — a deep evening raga of pathos and introspective longing
- Sympathetic strings resonating quietly beneath each phrase
- Tanpura drone — steady, holding the space open
- No percussion, no tabla — solo Sarangi with room to breathe
- 90 unbroken minutes at 432Hz tuning

⏱ Chapters
0:00    The weight you walked in with
20:00   Letting it surface
45:00   The deepest part
70:00   Something easing
85:00   A quieter close

🧠 How to use:
Press play, sit or lie down somewhere you won't be interrupted, and let the Sarangi carry the feeling instead of holding it yourself. You don't have to do anything. If the tears come, let them. That's the point.

⏱ Best for:
• Grief, heartache, and emotional processing
• Crying it out when you've been holding on too long
• Quiet evening time alone with a heavy feeling
• Journaling through something sad
• Winding down after a hard day

production_spec.notes: Raga Puriya — evening raga, komal Re + teevra Ma + komal Dha, the combination giving intense pathos and an introspective, longing quality (closely related to Marwa family). Solo emotional Sarangi: NO tabla, NO percussion — the instrument needs space, and rhythm would intrude on grief. Tanpura drone only, low underneath. Theta 5Hz binaural — deep relaxation for emotional processing (not sleep Delta, not morning Alpha). LUFS -14. The Sarangi is bowed and SOUNDS like a crying human voice via sliding meend and sympathetic resonance — but the brief must be explicit there is NO actual human voice / no vocals / no humming. EMOTIONAL TAG ROTATION (team reference, one strong metaphor per clip): clip 1: 'like the sound is crying so you don't have to hold it in alone' · clip 2: 'the weight finally finding somewhere to go' · clip 3: 'tender sorrow allowed to surface, then ease'. 90min = 3-4 Suno clips + loop extension.
